findings.title: MCP-for-Stata package-install tool permits command injection
findings.concise_factual_summary: MCP-for-Stata before 1.19.0 concatenates user-controlled input into a Stata command in the ado_package_install MCP tool. A caller who can invoke the tool or Python API can inject newline-delimited Stata commands, including shell escapes, leading to OS command execution as the Stata-MCP server user. Version 1.19.0 patches the issue.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with project advisory and release reference
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SepineTam mcp-for-stata before 1.19.0; ado_package_install MCP tool and equivalent Python API.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A default MCP tool converts package-management input into local command execution, showing how agent tool affordances can cross from data-plane actions into host-level code execution.

findings.title: CKAN MCP Server DNS-resolution SSRF bypass reaches cloud metadata
findings.concise_factual_summary: CKAN MCP Server before 0.4.108 validates only the supplied hostname string in validateServerUrl and does not resolve DNS before making outbound requests. A caller-supplied server_url whose hostname resolves to an internal address can pass validation and reach loopback or cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254. The advisory identifies this as a third bypass of the same guard and version 0.4.108 as the fix.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release reference
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ondata CKAN MCP Server before 0.4.108; SSRF guard for caller-supplied server_url.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent-facing data retrieval connectors need egress controls based on final resolved destinations, not input strings, especially when tools can reach cloud metadata services.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad CKAN MCP Server catalog context routes upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General connector egress-governance practice routes upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the SSRF bypass chain and fixed-version evidence here.

findings.title: NotebookLM MCP vault export permits path traversal
findings.concise_factual_summary: NotebookLM MCP versions 1.6.0 through 2.0.2 expose a path traversal in POST /batch-to-vault and the batch_to_vault MCP tool. Attacker-controlled vault_dir and slug_prefix values can write Markdown and JSON outside the intended vault. Version 2.0.3 sanitizes slug_prefix and supports containment when NOTEBOOKLM_VAULT_ROOT is configured; containment is not enabled when that variable is unset.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: roomi-fields notebooklm-mcp versions 1.6.0 through 2.0.2; batch-to-vault HTTP endpoint and MCP tool.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An LLM-facing export tool can turn untrusted generated content or tool arguments into filesystem writes unless the server enforces a fixed vault root and path containment.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: NotebookLM and MCP server catalog context routes upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General local-vault and tool-output practice routes upstream if framed as developer workflow.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the path traversal, export-tool, and mitigation boundary here.

findings.confidence_notes: High. CVE Services and NVD agree, and the GitHub advisory is the primary project advisory.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify whether version 2.0.3 has a release tag and whether NOTEBOOKLM_VAULT_ROOT should be treated as required hardening.

findings.title: Hatchet AI-agent workflow platform discloses tenant data and credentials across multiple paths
findings.concise_factual_summary: Hatchet disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in a platform for background tasks, AI agents, and durable workflows. The set includes an SNS UnsubscribeConfirmation SSRF path that can reach EC2 metadata, OAuth state reuse that can bind a victim session to an attacker-controlled identity, durable-task event-log APIs missing tenant scoping, callback delivery resolving task UUIDs without tenant identity, and worker-status polling missing a tenant filter. Fixed versions vary across 0.91.1, 0.95.3, and 0.106.1.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability records with GitHub advisory and patch references for at least part of the cluster
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Hatchet before 0.91.1 for SSRF, OAuth, and one event-log issue; before 0.95.3 for callback routing; before 0.106.1 for worker-status durable-event tenant filtering.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Durable agent workflow systems carry tenant identity, event logs, callbacks, OAuth identity, and cloud credentials; missing tenant filters or signed-field coverage can expose agent state and infrastructure secrets.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Hatchet product context routes upstream if cataloged.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General durable workflow and background task practice routes upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep tenant-boundary, SSRF, identity, and event-log exposure analysis here.

findings.title: MaxKB AI assistant exposes tools, chats, applications, models, sandbox, and cloud credentials
findings.concise_factual_summary: MaxKB disclosed a large September 21 cluster affecting enterprise AI assistant authorization, MCP tool usage, chat APIs, workflow application invocation, knowledge import, model-parameter updates, chat share links, AWS Bedrock credential handling, and sandbox escape controls. Several records have no fixed version as of review; others identify fixes in 2.10.5-lts or 2.10.6-lts.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability records with selected GitHub advisories and release references
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: 1Panel-dev MaxKB versions from 2.0.0 through 2.10.6-lts depending on CVE; affected areas include workspace tool grants, MCP endpoints, workflow nodes, application IDs, knowledge documents, model parameters, chat shares, AWS credentials, SandboxShellBackend, and ToolExecutor LD_PRELOAD hooks.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster shows repeated authorization gaps around agent tools, MCP configurations, application references, model credentials, and sandbox enforcement in an enterprise assistant, directly affecting least privilege and delegated authority.

findings.title: Chartbrew AI query tool can bypass read-only SQL controls
findings.concise_factual_summary: Chartbrew before 5.2.2 has two AI-orchestrator query issues. runQuery() uses a short SQL keyword blocklist for read-only enforcement, allowing dangerous statements or database functions not in the list. A second flaw interpolates the AI tool row_limit parameter into a LIMIT clause without runtime integer validation, so a model-influenced non-integer value can append SQL after the earlier keyword check. Version 5.2.2 fixes the issues.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability records with GitHub advisory, patch, and release reference
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An AI data-analysis tool that connects to live databases must enforce semantic query authorization, not a small blocklist or unchecked model-controlled parameters.

findings.title: Feast privileged CI workflow exposes AI feature-store cloud credentials
findings.concise_factual_summary: Feast before 0.65.0 uses pull_request_target with the synchronize event in pr_integration_tests.yml and preserves approval labels across newly pushed commits. A fork contributor can obtain approval for a benign revision and then run changed code in privileged make targets, exposing GCP, AWS, and Snowflake credentials. Version 0.65.0 fixes the workflow issue.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release reference
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Feast before 0.65.0; privileged GitHub Actions PR integration workflow for an AI and machine-learning feature store.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI/ML infrastructure supply chains often carry cloud and data-platform credentials; privileged CI on forked code can disclose downstream training, feature, and data credentials.

findings.title: 1millionbot AI Chat Platform permits limited client-side XSS
findings.concise_factual_summary: 1millionbot AI Chat Platform has an XSS issue in client-side rendering. An unauthenticated remote user can send messages containing Markdown syntax and unsanitized content blocks that render external hyperlinks in the web interface. The record states the impact is limited to the user's own interactive session and does not identify compromise of internal infrastructure, third-party data, or admin panels.
findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database record; low-impact AI chat surface
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: 1millionbot AI Chat Platform client-side rendering engine; affected versions not identified in fetched evidence.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Even limited chat-rendering XSS is relevant to AI security because chat UIs display untrusted model/user content and can become a content-trust boundary, though this record currently reports constrained impact.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep only the AI chat rendering boundary and low-impact caveat here.
